title: vGWAS basic tutorial
text: use vGWAS package, course, R environment required. Visit: http://www.r-project.org install R operating system. Start R R console, type following command install package dependencies first: Now package installed R library.

title: vGWAS basic tutorial
text: Load library R console, open vignette command: Nine main functions package ready use: bfmedian.test brown.forsythe.tes getMAF vGWAS vGWASparallel vGWAS.gc vGWAS.variance plot (S3 method vGWAS object) summary (S3 method vGWAS object) Run following commands load example data: pheno numeric vector simulated phenotypic values. running:  command: shows exactly number markers five simulated chromosomes. pre-filter geno.matrix data minor-allele-frequency, use getMAF function follows: Now, objects loaded R ready vGWA scan, can done using single command: progress bar indicate progress scan pB set TRUE. can run using multiple cores. Note: using vGWASparallel function one need specify, SNPs geno.matrix columns (geno.snp = "col") rows (geno.snp = "row") scan finished, output statistics returned list object vgwa, belongs class ‘vGWAS’. object structure belonging class ‘vGWAS’ can directly passed S3 method function plot. instance, simply run following command, can plot results vgwa:  produces Figure 2. clear peak Bonferroni corrected threshold (dashed orange line). Regarding marker gave highest score, heritability explained mean variance can split calculated via: output can also stored assigning function call object.
code: library(vGWAS) data(pheno) data(geno) data(chr) data(map) hist(pheno, breaks = 30, density = 15, col = "darkred") table(chr) #> chr #>    1    2    3    4    5  #> 5000 3000 4000 2000 6000 data(geno) dim(geno) #> [1]    93 20000 maf <- getMAF(geno.matrix = geno, geno.snp = "col") geno.maf <- geno[, maf > 0.05] dim(geno.maf) #> [1]    93 19075 chr.maf <- chr[maf > 0.05] map.maf <- map[maf > 0.05] vgwa <- vGWAS(   phenotype = pheno,   geno.matrix = geno,   marker.map = map,   chr.index = chr,   pB = FALSE) #vgwa <- vGWASparallel( #  phenotype = pheno, #  geno.matrix = geno, #  geno.snp = "col", #  marker.map = map, #  chr.index = chr, #  pB = FALSE, #  ncores = 2) plot(vgwa) #> nominal significance threshold with Bonferroni correction for 20000 tests are calculated. # get marker with lowest p.value marker.lowest <- vgwa[["p.value"]] == min(vgwa[["p.value"]]) vGWAS.variance(   phenotype = pheno,   marker.genotype = geno[, marker.lowest]) #> variance explained by the mean part of model: #> 4.2 % #> variance explained by the variance part of model: #> 23.06 % #> variance explained in total: #> 27.26 % #> $vm #>         C  #> 0.1026317  #>  #> $vv #>         C  #> 0.5628937  #>  #> $ve #>       C  #> 1.77584  #>  #> $vp #>        C  #> 2.441366

title: Variance Genome-wide Association (parallel) — vGWASparallel
text: phenotype numeric logical vector phenotyic values. geno.matrix matrix data.frame sparseMatrix individuals columns markers rows (geno.snp = "row") individuals rows markers columns (geno.snp = "col"). marker.map numeric vector giving marker map positions chromosome. chr.index numeric vector giving chromosome index marker. geno.snp individuals columns markers rows use "row" else individuals rows markers columns use "col" method test method use (default = bfmedian). Default set Brown-Forsythe's Test Equality Variances using group medians. 31 tests available via onewaytests package: Alvandi's F test ("af"), Alexander-Govern test ("ag"), Alvandi's generalized p-value ("agp"), One-way analysis variance ("aov"), Approximate F test ("ap"), Adjusted Welch's heteroscedastic F test ("aw"), B square test ("b2"), Brown-Forsythe test ("bf"), Box F test ("box"), Cochran test ("cochran"), Generalized tests equivalent Parametric Bootstrap ("gtb"), Generalized tests equivalent Fiducial tests ("gtf"), Variance homogeneity tests ("homog"), James second order test ("james"), Johansen F test ("johansen"), Kruskal-Wallis test ("kw"), Modified Brown-Forsythe test ("mbf"), Mann-Whitney U test ("mw"), Anderson-Darling normility test ("nor_ad"), Cramer-vin Mises normility test ("nor_cvm"), Kolmogorov-Smirnov normility test ("nor_ks"), Pearson Chi-square normility test ("nor_pct"), Shapiro-Wilk normility test ("nor_sw"), Shapiro-Francia normility test ("nor_sf"), Permutation F test ("pf"), Scott-Smith test ("ss"), Student's t-test ("st"), Welch-Aspin test ("wa"), Welch's heteroscedastic F test trimmed means Winsorized variances ("welch"), Weerahandi's generalized F test ("wgf"), Welch's t-test ("wt"). test.alpha level significance assess statistical difference. Default set alpha = 0.05. test.na.rm logical value indicating whether NA values stripped computation proceeds. Default us set TRUE. p.adjust.method correction method (default = "none"). 8 p-value correction methods available via p.adjust function: "holm", "hochberg", "hommel", "bonferroni", "BH", "", "fdr", "none" include.het specify heterozygous calls split added equally homozygous ref alt counts (default = FALSE) pB show progress bar ncores number cores parallelize (default = 1)
